name: Dredge Mining Collective Underwater Resource Extraction Platform
product_name: Dredge Mining Collective Underwater Resource Extraction Platform
description: An autonomous underwater mining system that operates on the ocean floor, extracting mineral resources from hydrothermal vents, manganese nodules, and submarine geological formations. The UREP deploys remotely operated vehicles and autonomous extractors to depths exceeding 6,000 meters, processing raw materials on-site and transporting refined minerals to surface collection vessels. The platform accesses mineral wealth that land-based mining cannot reach and operates in international waters where territorial regulations are ambiguous at best.
social_impact: The UREP has opened a new resource frontier that no single entity controls, triggering a slow-motion race for ocean floor mineral rights that existing legal frameworks are not equipped to manage. Dredge's early mover advantage gives them de facto control of the most productive sites, and their willingness to operate in legal gray zones means that competing claims are backed by operational presence rather than legal title.
story_hooks: A UREP operation has discovered an artificial structure on the ocean floor at 4,000 meters depth — the structure predates any known deep-water construction capability and its purpose is unknown.

Dredge's UREP extraction is disrupting a hydrothermal vent ecosystem that hosts unique extremophile organisms — the organisms produce compounds with extraordinary medical potential, and the mining is destroying them before they can be studied.
